question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-y+2z &=8 \\ -2x+2y-3z &=-11 \\ x+z &=9.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ -2 & 2 & -3 & -11 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 9\end{array}\right].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ -2 & 2 & -3 & -11 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 9\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 5 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 9\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 1\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 1\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 5\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-y+2z &=8 \\ y-z &=1 \\ z &=5,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The third equation $z=5$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-(5) &=1\,⟹\,y=6.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $y=6$ and $z=5$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x-(6)+2(5) &=8\,⟹\,x=4.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=4$, $y=6$, and $z=5.$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 5 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 & 4 & 9\end{array}\right].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 5 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 & 4 & 9\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 & 4 & 9\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -3 & -2 & 7\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -3 & -2 & 7\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & -3 & -2 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 2\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we multiply the $2$nd row by $-\frac{1}{3}$ and the $3$rd row by $\frac{1}{2}$ to get

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & -3 & -2 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 2\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{2}{3} & -\frac{7}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 2\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{2}{3} & -\frac{7}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}4 & -4 & -12 & 8 \\ -1 & 1 & 10 & -5 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & -6\end{array}\right].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}4 & -4 & -12 & 8 \\ -1 & 1 & 10 & -5 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & -6\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -3 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 & 10 & -5 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & -6\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 7 & -3 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & -6\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 7 & -3 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & -6\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 7 & -3\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we multiply the $2$nd row by $\frac{1}{3}$ and the $3$rd row by $\frac{1}{7}$ to get

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 7 & -3\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 7 & -3\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :=\frac{1}{7}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{3}{7}\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-3x+6y-3z &=18 \\ -4x+8y-3z &=2 \\ y-4z &=-3.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-3 & 6 & -3 & 18 \\ -4 & 8 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & -3\end{array}\right].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-3 & 6 & -3 & 18 \\ -4 & 8 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & -3\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & :=-\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 1 & -6 \\ -4 & 8 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & -3\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 1 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -22 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & -3\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 1 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -22 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & -3\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 1 & -6 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -22\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y+z &=-6 \\ y-4z &=-3 \\ z &=-22,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The third equation $z=-22$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-4(-22) &=-3\,⟹\,y=-91.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $y=-91$ and $z=-22$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x-2(-91)+(-22) &=-6\,⟹\,x=-166.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=-166$, $y=-91$, and $z=-22.$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ -2 & -2 & 5 & -2 \\ 3 & 4 & -1 & 1\end{array}\right].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ -2 & -2 & 5 & -2 \\ 3 & 4 & -1 & 1\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 3 & 4 & -1 & 1\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & -8\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & -8\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & -8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+y-2z &=3 \\ y+5z &=-8 \\ z &=4,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The third equation $z=4$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y+5(4) &=-8\,⟹\,y=-28.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $y=-28$ and $z=4$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x+(-28)-2(4) &=3\,⟹\,x=39.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=39$, $y=-28$, and $z=4.$ Or, in vector form $⟨39,-28,4⟩.$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-2 & 2 & -6 & 4 \\ 5 & -5 & 16 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1\end{array}\right].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-2 & 2 & -6 & 4 \\ 5 & -5 & 16 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & :=-\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 3 & -2 \\ 5 & -5 & 16 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-5){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 11 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 11 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 11\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-y+3z &=-2 \\ y+2z &=-1 \\ z &=11,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The third equation $z=11$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y+2(11) &=-1\,⟹\,y=-23.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $y=-23$ and $z=11$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x-(-23)+3(11) &=-2\,⟹\,x=-58.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=-58$, $y=-23$, and $z=11.$ Or, in vector form, $⟨-58,-23,11⟩.$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}3x-6y+3z &=-6 \\ 2x-4y+3z &=-1 \\ 2y-4z &=2.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}3 & -6 & 3 & -6 \\ 2 & -4 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & 2\end{array}\right].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}3 & -6 & 3 & -6 \\ 2 & -4 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & 2\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 1 & -2 \\ 2 & -4 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & 2\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & 2\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & 2\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we multiply the $2$nd row by $\frac{1}{2}$ to get

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & -6 & 1 & 3 \\ -1 & 4 & -1 & -5\end{array}\right].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & -6 & 1 & 3 \\ -1 & 4 & -1 & -5\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & 4 & -1 & -5\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -4\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -4\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-3y &=1 \\ y-z &=-4 \\ z &=1,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The third equation $z=1$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-(1) &=-4\,⟹\,y=-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $y=-3$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x-3(-3) &=1\,⟹\,x=-8.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=-8$, $y=-3$, and $z=1.$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+2y-z &=4 \\ -3x-6y+4z &=-8 \\ 3x+7y-z &=10.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & 4 \\ -3 & -6 & 4 & -8 \\ 3 & 7 & -1 & 10\end{array}\right].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & 4 \\ -3 & -6 & 4 & -8 \\ 3 & 7 & -1 & 10\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 3 & 7 & -1 & 10\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -2\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -2\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+2y-z &=4 \\ y+2z &=-2 \\ z &=4,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The third equation $z=4$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y+2(4) &=-2\,⟹\,y=-10.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $y=-10$ and $z=4$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x+2(-10)-(4) &=4\,⟹\,x=28.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=28$, $y=-10$, and $z=4.$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}5 & 20 & -10 & -5 \\ -2 & -8 & 6 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & 12\end{array}\right].

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}5 & 20 & -10 & -5 \\ -2 & -8 & 6 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & 12\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 4 & -2 & -1 \\ -2 & -8 & 6 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & 12\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 4 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & 12\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 4 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & 12\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 4 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & 12 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we multiply the $2$nd row by $\frac{1}{3}$ and the $3$rd row by $\frac{1}{2}$ to get

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 4 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & 12 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 4 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 4 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+6y-3z &=-1 \\ -2x-12y+8z &=1 \\ -x-5y+4z &=2.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 6 & -3 & -1 \\ -2 & -12 & 8 & 1 \\ -1 & -5 & 4 & 2\end{array}\right].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 6 & -3 & -1 \\ -2 & -12 & 8 & 1 \\ -1 & -5 & 4 & 2\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 6 & -3 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -1 \\ -1 & -5 & 4 & 2\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 6 & -3 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 6 & -3 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 6 & -3 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -1\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we multiply the $3$rd row by $\frac{1}{2}$ to get

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 6 & -3 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -1\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 6 & -3 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{2}\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x+4y-4z &=4 \\ x+2y-z &=-1 \\ y+3z &=1.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & 4 & -4 & 4 \\ 1 & 2 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 1\end{array}\right].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & 4 & -4 & 4 \\ 1 & 2 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 1\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -2 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 1\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 1\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 1\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -3\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+2y-2z &=2 \\ y+3z &=1 \\ z &=-3,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The third equation $z=-3$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y+3(-3) &=1\,⟹\,y=10.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $y=10$ and $z=-3$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x+2(10)-2(-3) &=2\,⟹\,x=-24.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=-24$, $y=10$, and $z=-3.$ Or, in vector form, $⟨-24,10,-3⟩.$
